proposed_from.topic: Necessary-and-sufficient DOG-invariant total-effect certification under simultaneous latent confounding and measurement error. In Yang et al.'s canonical separable, minimal, rank-faithful linear LV-SEM-ME with known observation labels, characterize the complete pairwise total-effect image over every minimum-edge DOG model; prove the normalized-column projection, singleton minor iff, attaining countermodels, polynomial global minimum-completion algorithm, and confidence-region inference. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: exact reductions, witnesses, destructive checks, and all remaining gaps are recorded in <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_lvsemme_dog_effect_certificate.md. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: polynomial constrained minimum completion under coupled downstream cancellations. EARLY KILL TEST: recover and certify the recorded faithful 12-edge plateau optimum.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest population comparator is Tramontano et al. (2024): Theorems 3.3 and 3.8 give complete generic total-effect criteria in lvLiNGAM, and Theorem 3.11 gives a cubic graphical procedure. The proposal does not claim the normalized mixing-column idea as new and must reproduce their unknown-graph criterion on the shared real generic no-measurement subclass. The strict delta is the complete image for the mixed DOG transformation: known observation labels map each intervention label to either one cogent candidate group or a fixed singleton-mleaf branch; within a cogent group the label may switch between center and mleaf, pivot normalization changes jointly with the selected structural noise, and only pairs attained inside a globally minimum reconstruction enter the image. The zero and minor comparisons for singletonness are presented only as transparent algebraic consequences of that image. Yang et al. (2026) provide the real mixed equivalence class on a stratumwise generic domain but enumerate every joint assignment and analyze one four-node effect. The computational kernel asks for the exact algorithm-versus-hardness classification of rational minimum completion; the faithful plateau establishes nonadditivity but does not prejudge either branch. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026) and Wienoebst et al. (2023) inform possible positive techniques without subsuming the coupled completion problem. No inferential construction or coverage-transfer identity is counted toward novelty.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorem 3; Algorithm 2; Proposition 6; complexity paragraph after Proposition 7; Appendix A.2; Appendix A.4; Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Construct a polynomial globally constrained minimum-completion algorithm and use its projected minimizers to compute every pairwise DOG effect image and iff certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Algorithm 2's Cartesian loop over all row and column assignments by fraction-free group elimination with a polynomial rank signature or a polynomial separation oracle.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for DOG minimum completion, LV-SEM-ME polynomial recovery, and center-noise sparsity optimization found only Yang et al.'s enumerator and algorithms for different equivalence structures.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from Yang et al. because Proposition 6 says DOG models are exactly the minimum-edge AOG models.
seed_details.rebuttal: Proposition 6 identifies the optimum set but Algorithm 2 still enumerates exponentially many joint choices; the faithful twelve-edge plateau proves that independent group scoring and strict coordinate descent do not compute it.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The named focal object is \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\), the algorithm must certify a global optimum, and the open construction has a concrete elimination or separation-oracle handle.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Section 5; Appendix A.2 center and noise switches; Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the complete effect image by normalized feasible source columns and prove singleton identification if and only if the corresponding minors vanish.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After the center/noise switch construction, compute the full intervention column from the choice-specific normalized block inverse instead of analyzing only the four-node union coefficient.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for LV-SEM-ME effect image and DOG-invariant total effects found no paper beyond Yang et al.'s special union example.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from Tramontano et al. because normalized mixing columns already characterize total effects under latent confounding.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their admissible ambiguity is a source-column swap without measured-variable center reassignment; a measured intervention may become an mleaf, contributing zero, and its pivot changes jointly with the selected noise column.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The result includes both directions, exact attaining models, the complete finite image, and the mixed-model reduction; it is not a normalized-column observation alone.

seed_details.kernel: Derive the exact distance-to-decision-variety margin for local constancy of the singleton DOG certificate and a matching local impossibility result as the margin vanishes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace qualitative nonzero rank minors by singular-value and normalized-minor perturbation inequalities that also protect the ordering of global completion scores.
seed_details.destination_search: Strong-faithfulness searches found conditional-independence margins but no quantitative margin for mixing-column minors coupled to minimum DOG completion.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from standard matrix perturbation theory and strong faithfulness.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary perturbation bounds protect a fixed rank test, whereas the desired radius must simultaneously preserve support, all decisive minors, the global minimum set, and the set-valued effect projection.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposed margin is a derived observable-parameter object with both stability and impossibility directions, not a stronger assumption chosen to force consistency.

seed_details.destination_search: Post-discovery inference searches located DAG and CPDAG union intervals, but no overcomplete-ICA region propagated through minimum-edge DOG selection.

seed_details.destination_search: Tramontano et al. derive cumulant estimators for specific proxy and underspecified-instrument lvLiNGAM designs, while Dai et al. treat measurement error without simultaneous latent confounding; no general mixed-model region was found.

proposed_from.literature_map: The direct anchor thread is Yang et al. (2026). Definition 2 fixes the canonical mixed model, Assumptions 1, 3, and 4 supply separability, rank faithfulness, and minimality, Theorem 3 identifies only the DOG class, Algorithm 2 enumerates all center and noise choices, Proposition 6 identifies DOG members by global minimum edge count, Appendix A.2 gives the simultaneous switch construction, and Section 5 treats one four-node effect. The effect-image thread is Salehkaleybar et al. (2020), Section 4, and Tramontano et al. (2024), Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, and 3.11. Those papers establish that projecting observational ambiguity onto total effects can yield complete iff criteria and efficient certification, but their transformations have neither measurement labels nor the possibility that a labeled intervention becomes an mleaf. The algorithmic thread is Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026), Theorems 3.6 and 4.2--4.3, where determinant ranks become nonintersecting-path maxima and then maximum flow, and Wienoebst et al. (2023), where local equivalence moves support linear-delay MEC enumeration. Neither thread optimizes Yang's rational edge-count reconstruction under cancellations across multiple groups. The inference thread is Chang et al. (2026), Algorithm 2 and Theorem 2, Bellot (2024), the statistical-uncertainty remark after Example 3, Robins et al. (2003), and Zhang and Spirtes (2012). These establish the value of union confidence objects and the danger of qualitative faithfulness near decision boundaries, but none supplies an aligned overcomplete-ICA mixing region. Saeed et al. (2020), Jung et al. (2021), Tramontano et al. (2025), and Dai et al. (2022) are adjacent estimation threads with nonnested model restrictions. No closer public paper subsumes the proposed coupled minimum-completion kernel.
